title: Placing a block builds it instantly anywhere: no build plan, builder travel or construction progress

path.to: Campaign -> Serpulo -> Ground Zero -> select a buildable block -> place it far from the player core
godot: input::queue::BuildQueue exists but is referenced only by core tests

java: gradlew desktop:run; fresh Serpulo/Ground Zero; select the conveyor (or mechanical drill); click a tile ~20 tiles from the core
a ghost plan appears, the player mech travels to it and constructs it (ConstructBlock with an increasing progress value); the finished block exists only once progress reaches 1
godot: launch Ground Zero; select a block; click the same far tile; screenshot + get_state_json for that tile in the same frame
the finished block is present immediately, with no queued plan, no construct progress and no unit travel; the core's items are charged at once
compare: inspect the target tile and the player unit's plan list after the click: Java holds a BuildPlan plus a ConstructBlock with progress < 1; the port holds the final block id and no plan

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: mind-gdext/src/input/desktop.rs commit_place bypasses InputState::flush_plans/BuildQueue and enqueues an instant SimCommand::Place, which sim/runtime.rs applies as a finished block (runtime.rs:21 admits there is no builder-unit progress path)
plan.approach: 1) Route the desktop release path through DesktopController::flush / InputState::flush_plans (or queue.add_build) instead of hand-building SimCommands in commit_place. 2) Add a wire command that queues a plan on the player unit's BuilderComp (e.g. SimCommand::AddBuild {x,y,block,rotation,team,front}) instead of placing the tile, keeping valid_place gating and same-position replacement/ConstructBlock progress carry-over. 3) Run the plan-11 builder update (ai/types/builder.rs update_builder + approach/ConstructBlock creation) for the player unit each tick, then let construction progress finish the block. 4) Leave SelectBlock/Place instant only for editor/API paths. Check: headless scenario asserting the target tile stays air and a plan is queued right after the command, and the block appears only after the expected build ticks.
plan.narrow_check: extension scenario `spine_place_buildplan`: after SimCommand::AddBuild the tile is air/ConstructBlock with progress 0 and the unit's plan list has one entry; after N ticks the block id matches and the plan is gone

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (input-controls): S2 high confidence. Player impact: construction economy and builder-unit gameplay are absent - any block can be dropped anywhere for free the instant the mouse is released, so distance, build speed and the build queue never matter. Context: plan 24 sec 7 input residual 'Real plan-11 BuilderComp call-through (the input::queue::BuildQueue seam stands in)'; the live gdext path never calls InputState::flush_plans (grep: only the doc comment at desktop.rs:178). In-engine verification pending.

title: Schematic copy mode is dead: F does nothing, so an area cannot be copied into select plans, flipped or placed

path.to: Campaign -> Ground Zero -> press F and drag a rectangle over existing buildings (and, separately, B for rebuild select)
java: DesktopInput.pollInputPlayer: F/B keyTap starts the select rect, keyRelease creates the schematic and fills selectPlans
selectPlans follow the cursor, Z/X flip, wheel rotates, left click flushes them
godot: input::line rotate_plans/flip_plans are reachable only from the unwired mobile bridge

java: play groundZero; hold F, drag over the core, release: a ghost copy of the region follows the cursor; scroll rotates it, Z/X flip it, left click queues it for the builder
godot: same input path: push key_down 'f' (or press F), drag with left mouse, release; call get_input_state_json()
mode stays 'none', select_plans stays 0 and no placement ghost appears; Z/X and the wheel do nothing to any selection
compare: after the F-drag, Java's InputHandler.selectPlans.size > 0 and a ghost is drawn at the cursor; the port's select_plans stays 0 in every state dump

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: mind-gdext/src/input/desktop.rs dispatch_action/left_press/scroll never implement the schematic-select / select-plan mode that mind-core already models (InputState::select_plans, InputState::schematic_select, rebuild_select)
plan.approach: 1) Add dispatch arms for schematic_select/rebuild_select: on key_down record the raw start tile, on key_up (with a moved cursor) create the schematic via game/schematics.rs create(rect) + to_plans into state.select_plans (B uses MobileController::rebuild_area). 2) On MouseMove while select_plans is non-empty shift every plan by the cursor delta (upstream schematicX/Y), and refresh PreviewState. 3) Add schematic_flip_x/schematic_flip_y arms calling line.rs flip_plans, and make scroll rotate select plans when non-empty. 4) On left press with select_plans non-empty commit them through InputState::flush_plans/BuildQueue (same seam as the instant-build finding), and clear on clear_building/deselect. Check: headless input scenario asserting plan count/positions after F-drag, cursor shift, flip and commit.
plan.narrow_check: new scenario `input_schematic_select`: F-drag over a 3x3 block region yields select_plans of the expected size, a cursor move shifts them by the delta, flip_plans mirrors x, and a click commits them to the queue

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (input-controls): S3 high confidence. Player impact: the blueprint copy/paste workflow is unavailable - the copy half (F drag -> select plans) and the place half (click to commit, flip Z/X, wheel rotate) both have no live entry point, so saved schematics can only exist as data. Distinct from the payload and RTS-unit findings (PAR ledger / code-scan units-ai); this is the build-plan select mode. The Schematics dialog surface itself is another agent's domain. In-engine verification pending.

title: Focus/lock guards are dead in the live client: wheel-over-UI zooms the camera and an active input lock does not stop world input

path.to: Campaign -> Ground Zero -> press F8 to open the console (or set a lock through the Input API) -> scroll / click
java: DesktopInput.update zoom gate: hasScroll/chat/console/dialog suppress scaleCamera
DesktopInput: locked() skips pollInputPlayer and the updateMovement block
godot: MindInput stores FocusState/InputLocks via set_ui_focus/set_locks but nothing reads them
DesktopBridge.scroll consults only ui_dialog; pan_axis only text_focus/ui_dialog
mind-core FocusGuards (focus.rs) is referenced only by headless scenarios and the unused DesktopController::handle_scroll

java: open the console (F8) or hover a scroll pane and scroll: the camera zoom is suppressed; with an input lock active (mod addLock / renderer.isCutscene()) DesktopInput skips pollInputPlayer and updateMovement, so no pan or place happens
godot: open the console (F8), scroll the wheel over its output: the console scrolls AND the world camera zooms (compare MindCamera2D zoom before/after)
MCP: eval get_node('/root/Spine/Input').set_locks('["cutscene"]'); then hold W and click a world tile: the camera pans and the tile is placed while get_input_state_json reports locks ["cutscene"]
compare: same wheel/lock input in Java changes no camera scale while the console is shown and performs no world action while locked; the port's zoom value changes and the placed tile appears

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: MindInput keeps self.focus/self.locks only for the state dump (mod.rs:553/570) and DesktopBridge re-derives two ad-hoc probes (text_focus/ui_dialog) instead of consulting mind-core FocusGuards
plan.approach: 1) Pass a FocusGuards value (FocusState + InputLocks) into DesktopBridge::handle/scroll/pan_axis instead of the two ad-hoc booleans. 2) Gate the wheel with FocusGuards::blocks_zoom (has_scroll/chat_shown/console_shown/has_dialog) so scroll never zooms through UI; gate pan/zoom with blocks_camera (locked||typing). 3) Gate place/break/mine with can_place/can_shoot, and clear state.block when locked (InputHandler.update locked() branch). 4) Have plan 14 push a real UiFocus each frame (has_scroll from the hovered Control type, chat/console from the fragments' is_shown, has_dialog from MindUi.dialog_stack); make MindCamera2D's logic cutscene set LockId::LogicCutscene so the camera and input agree. Check: extend input_focus_guards plus an MCP assertion that scroll with the console open leaves MindCamera2D zoom unchanged and set_locks('["cutscene"]') leaves pan_axis at zero and world clicks inert.
plan.narrow_check: cargo test -p mind-core input::focus + MCP: set_locks(['cutscene']) then pan_axis() == Vector2(0,0) and a world click leaves the tile unchanged; wheel over the open console leaves the camera zoom unchanged

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (input-controls): S3 high confidence on the dead seam, medium on the lock half's current reachability (no shipped path sets a lock yet; logic cutscene side effects are inert, so today the trigger is the MCP/direct set_locks or a future cutscene). Player impact: UI focus does not protect the camera (wheel over the console/scroll panes also zooms the world) and cutscene/lock states cannot gate input at all. Context: plan 24 sec 7 input residual 'Runtime reachability of desktop+mobile handlers, locked()/focus-guard branch parity'. DesktopController::handle_scroll (the core gated path) is never called by gdext. In-engine verification pending.

title: Gameplay hotkeys fire on the main menu: T opens the Schematics dialog and F8 the console before a game is started

path.to: Boot to the main menu and press T (schematics), F8 (console), E (pause building) or Q (clear building)
java: Control.update calls input.update() only inside if(state.isGame())
DesktopInput.update gating: minimap/planetMap/research/schematicMenu only when state.isGame()
godot: MindInput.input/process always dispatches binding actions to DesktopBridge
MindUi.open_dialog ignores the manifest menu_openable flag

java: gradlew desktop:run; at the main menu press T, F8, E, Q: nothing happens (input.update() is not called outside a game state and DesktopInput.update early-returns on state.isMenu())
godot: boot the client to the main menu; inject/press T: the Schematics dialog opens (MindUi dialog_stack becomes ['schematics']); press F8: the console fragment shows; press E: get_input_state_json().is_building flips
compare: same keys on the menu: Java dialog_stack stays empty and is_building stays true; the port opens dialogs and mutates placement state

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: MindInput has no game-state (is_game/is_menu) feed, so DesktopBridge::dispatch_action runs in every state; upstream only dispatches while state.isGame() and early-returns on state.isMenu()
plan.approach: 1) Expose the current game state to MindInput (e.g. a MindSimHost #[func] is_game()/state_name() over GameState/PlayState, or push it through the plan-14 UiFocus payload). 2) In MindInput::input/process, skip binding dispatch and world pointer handling when not in game (still run updateState-equivalent reset), mirroring Control.update's if(state.isGame()) gate. 3) On entering the menu, apply InputState::reset (clears command mode/selection/line plans) and reject open_dialog for manifest entries whose menu_openable is false. Check: MCP at boot asserts dialog_stack stays empty after inject_key('t') and that the same key opens the dialog once in a sector.
plan.narrow_check: MCP scenario: boot -> inject_key('t') -> MindUi.dialog_stack() == []; load Ground Zero -> inject_key('t') -> dialog_stack == ['schematics']

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (input-controls): S3 high confidence. Player impact: the main menu leaks gameplay interactions (dialogs/console/placement toggles open from the menu, and the manifest's menu_openable=false for schematics is not enforced), unlike Java where no binding is processed outside a game. This is the same guard-wiring family as the focus/lock finding but a distinct missing feed (game state, not FocusState). In-engine verification pending.

title: Rebinding an axis key (move_x/move_y/rotate/zoom) drops the second direction: one capture replaces the two-key pair

path.to: Main menu / in-game Settings -> Controls -> Rebind Keys -> Rebind on move_x -> press one key
java: KeybindDialog.rebind two-step axis flow: first key stored as minKey, dialog reopens for the second key, then Axis(minKey,newKey) is written
godot: keybind_dialog.gd _start_capture is a single one-key overlay for both kinds
MindInput.rebind_key -> bindings::rebind writes set_axis(id, None, Some(code)) for KeyKind::Axis
BindingState::set_axis replaces the whole pair, clearing the negative side

java: open Settings -> Controls -> Rebind Keys; click Rebind on move_x; press Q: the dialog stays open asking for the second key; press E: the key column shows 'Q / E' and both keys drive the axis
godot: same flow: press Q only; the capture closes immediately and the key column shows 'Q' (no '/ E')
after closing, only Q pans while the previous negative key (A) does nothing; user://keybinds.json stores an empty negative side for move_x
compare: keybinds_json move_x after the rebind: Java has a two-key Axis pair; the port reports negativeDisplay null and key_axis() only ever returns the positive direction

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: keybind_dialog.gd capture flow + mind-gdext bindings::rebind axis branch both assume one key per binding
plan.approach: 1) Mark axis entries in keybind_dialog.gd (entry.axis) and run the upstream two-step capture: first key becomes minKey, the overlay reopens with the @keybind.press.axis prompt, the second key applies the pair (scroll stays a valid first key). 2) Add an axis-aware apply path (e.g. MindInput.rebind_axis(name, negative, positive) or a JSON pair) that writes BindingState::set_axis with both sides instead of the current set_axis(id, None, Some(code)). 3) Keep reset/unbind semantics. Check: extend bindings::tests to assert a rebind of move_x to (q, e) round-trips through settings and reports both sides.
plan.narrow_check: cargo test -p mind-gdext bindings::tests (or a new core BindingState test) asserting set_axis/save/load keeps both keys; MCP: rebind move_x to Q then E and assert keybinds_json.move_x.negativeDisplay == 'Q' and .display == 'E'

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (input-controls): S3 high confidence. Player impact: rebinding any two-key axis (move_x, move_y, rotate, zoom) silently unbinds one direction and the dialog's key column loses the 'min / max' pair display; the single-key rebind path itself does apply live (same BindingState the bridge reads per event), which is why this is scoped to the axis flow. In-engine verification pending.
